summary: Build-time hardening of both images is correct and independently re-verified; two minor documentation defects, neither blocking.
notes: contract-check ok=true, no violations; not_checked: forbid.behaviors (judged by hand below).
acceptance-coverage status=pass, no gaps; AC-1..AC-5 all covered by blueprint scenarios.

Scope: exactly Dockerfile (+109/-0) and sidecar/Dockerfile (+121/-4), working tree clean at 22dc76e; the 4 deletions only reconcile the sidecar's now-false claim that diagnostic tools stay available after A-6 hardening. Nothing under deploy/, no compose file, no .env, no Rust/Go source: no collision with the concurrent HEX-068.

REVIEWER RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (not trusting the delegate's prose or 05-validation.json): both images rebuilt from scratch, exit 0. docker image inspect reports Config.User=10001:10001 for BOTH; adduser -u 10001 / addgroup -g 10001 are explicit literals; ENTRYPOINT stays exec-form ([/usr/local/bin/hexcell] and [/usr/local/bin/hexcell-sidecar]), so SIGTERM still reaches PID 1 for the A-2/A-3 ordered shutdown.

NFR-05 core invariant proven, not inferred: on a FRESH EMPTY named volume under --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges, the core creates and migrates sessions.db, knowledge_live.db and adapter_identity.db, and the sidecar creates sqlstore.db, identidad.db, outbox.db plus ipc/sidecar.sock (0600), all owned 10001:10001, both containers staying alive with no EROFS/EACCES. Both were then run CONCURRENTLY on ONE shared named volume: all five databases plus the socket coexist under the same UID with no permission error.

Read-only rootfs: nothing in either final stage needs a writable path outside /var/lib/hexcell. TMPDIR/SQLITE_TMPDIR redirect into the volume is the only mitigation applied; no PRAGMA temp_store or any other source change was smuggled in (forbid.behaviors respected).

Deliberate asymmetry preserved and verified by image export: the sidecar has the ca-certificates package (/usr/sbin/update-ca-certificates present, /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt survives shell removal), the core does NOT install it (update-ca-certificates absent; the bundle it does carry comes from alpine's base ca-certificates-bundle, not from a harmonising apk add). Ordering is correct: apk add ca-certificates at line 174, shell-removal RUN at line 265.

Shell removal genuine in both images: docker run --entrypoint /bin/sh fails for both. AC-5 comment blocks name read_only, cap_drop [ALL], no-new-privileges, the named volume and the optional tmpfs in BOTH files and explicitly defer them to HEX-068; none is implemented here, which is by design and not a gap.

Comment-accuracy audit against a live alpine:3 container: base is 3.24.1, highest system UID below 1000 is 405 (guest), nobody is 65534, no 10001 collision, and `apk del --no-network busybox-binsh` does exit 0 while removing nothing (refused because alpine-baselayout depends on it). Every measured claim in the new comments is true, including the named-volume-inherits-owner/mode fact that HEX-068's template depends on.

DEFECT (minor, documentation, both files): the justification for retaining apk-tools and /lib/apk/db states that 'la tarea 16 de la etapa A-6 audita la imagen contra ella'. Stage A-6 task 16 is 'Medir memoria y tamano de imagenes' (RSS via cgroup v2 plus image weight); no A-6 task schedules a CVE or vulnerability scan at all. The claim was inherited verbatim from this contract's own forbid.behaviors, so the invented forward-reference originates upstream, not with the implementer. Keeping apk-tools remains defensible; only the citation is wrong.

OBSERVATION (minor, both files): `apk del --no-network busybox-binsh` is a verified no-op deliberately retained as documentation of the path the contract prescribed, with the real removal done by `rm -f /bin/sh /bin/busybox`. The comment says so honestly, which is the right call, but it leaves an inert build step; a future task may drop it.

GUARD WEAKNESS (in this contract, not in the diff): verify command 1 satisfies its busybox-binsh check on a line that may be a comment, and its ca-certificates-ordering check resolved L_RM to comment line 250 rather than the RUN at 265, so the ordering guard would still pass if the RUN moved before the apk add. The substance is correct here; the guard is weaker than it looks.

EVIDENCE-QUALITY ISSUE FOR THE HUMAN (does not change the verdict): verify command 4 (AC-3) expands $ENVS through unquoted word-splitting. Reproducing it verbatim, the env vars never reached either container: both exited in about 200 ms on a config-validation error, the effective-UID probe was silently skipped by its own `[ "$PID" != "0" ]` guard, and the EROFS/EACCES log grep passed vacuously while the command still exited 0. 05-validation.json nevertheless records 'UID efectivo: 10001' for both images, an output this reviewer could not reproduce with the command as written. The underlying claim is nonetheless TRUE: re-run with explicit -e flags, both images start, run as effective UID 10001 and write their databases as described above. AC-3 is genuinely satisfied; only its recorded evidence is not reproducible.
